Topics. resource optimization / The manual cleanup of residual Shopify app code: uninstalling an app does not always remove its injected scripts. Merchants must search theme.liquid, head.liquid, and footer.liquid (using tools like the Shopify Theme File Search Chrome extension) for app names (e.g., "loox") and delete lingering <script> tags to prevent external server requests. Image optimization: restricting file sizes to under 1MB, using JPEG instead of PNG (unless transparency is required), and replacing heavy, animated GIFs with compressed MP4 videos using HTML <video> tags. Lazy loading mechanics: applying preload="none" to videos and loading="lazy" to off-screen images, but strictly avoiding lazy loading for above-the-fold assets (like hero images), which instead require a preload link in the <head> to minimize LCP. Font optimization: ensuring all @font-face CSS declarations include font-display: swap so the browser renders text in a system font immediately rather than remaining blank while the custom font downloads. Script execution order: appending defer or async attributes to non-essential JavaScript tags in theme.liquid so they do not block HTML parsing, with the explicit exception of tracking pixels, which must not be deferred. CSS optimization: using the media="print" onload="this.media='all'" trick to load non-critical stylesheets asynchronously.

Look for. The file paths to check for residual app code: theme.liquid, head.liquid, and footer.liquid. The specific file format that should replace animated GIFs: MP4 videos inside an HTML <video> tag. The specific CSS property required to prevent "flash of invisible text" when using custom fonts: font-display: swap inside the @font-face rule. The specific HTML attribute used to delay non-essential JavaScript execution until the DOM is loaded: defer. The specific HTML attribute trick to load non-critical CSS without blocking rendering: <link rel="stylesheet" href="..." media="print" onload="this.media='all'">.
